name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q01 - Animal husbandry dairying poultry apiculture and fisheries

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements regarding animal husbandry and allied practices:

Statement I: Animal husbandry includes poultry farming and fisheries in addition to the care and breeding of cattle, buffaloes, sheep, goats, pigs, horses, and camels.

Statement II: Mechanisation of milking, storage, and transport in modern dairy farms reduces the chance of direct contact of the produce with the handler.

Statement III: Selection of disease-free and suitable breeds, proper and safe farm conditions, proper feed and water, and hygiene and health care are important components of poultry farm management.

Statement IV: Beehives can only be maintained in dense forest habitats and cannot be kept in courtyards, on verandahs, or on roofs.

Statement V: Catla, Rohu, and common carp are common freshwater fishes, whereas Pomfrets are marine fishes.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animal husbandry integrates livestock rearing, dairy and poultry management, apiculture, and fisheries using scientific hygiene and habitat practices.

Step 2: Evaluation of Scope, Dairy Mechanisation, and Poultry Care
Extended animal husbandry includes poultry farming and fisheries alongside traditional livestock. In modern dairy farms, mechanisation of milking, storage, and transport minimises direct contact between the produce and handlers. In poultry farm management, selecting disease-free suitable breeds, maintaining safe farm conditions, providing proper feed and water, and ensuring hygiene and health care are essential. All three of these claims are true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Apiculture Location and Fish Habitats
Bee-keeping is not labour-intensive and can be practised anywhere with sufficient bee pastures, including courtyards, house verandahs, or roofs; restricting beehives to dense forests is false. Conversely, Catla, Rohu, and common carp are indeed common freshwater fishes while Pomfrets are marine fishes, making that claim true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims covering the scope of animal husbandry, dairy mechanisation, poultry management, and freshwater/marine fish examples are correct, whereas the habitat restriction on bee-keeping is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and V are correct.
Statements I, II, IV, and V are correct.
Statements II, III, IV, and V are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q02 - Animal breeds inbreeding depression out-breeding and MOET

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following five statements regarding animal breeding:

Statement I: A breed is a group of animals related by descent and similar in most characters such as general appearance, features, size, and configuration.

Statement II: Continued close inbreeding increases fertility and productivity indefinitely without causing any inbreeding depression.

Statement III: Out-breeding encompasses out-crossing, cross-breeding, and interspecific hybridisation.

Statement IV: In cross-breeding, superior males of one breed are mated with superior females of another breed, and the resulting hybrids may be used directly for commercial production or subjected to inbreeding and selection to develop new stable breeds.

Statement V: In Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer Technology (MOET), cows are administered progesterone-like hormones to yield 1–2 eggs per cycle.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animal breeding balances homozygosity and hybrid vigour using defined breeds, inbreeding, out-breeding strategies, and hormonal super ovulation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Breed Definition and Inbreeding Depression
Animals related by descent and sharing general appearance, features, size, and configuration constitute a breed, making that claim true. However, continued close inbreeding usually reduces fertility and productivity, a phenomenon termed inbreeding depression; claiming it increases fertility indefinitely is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Out-breeding, Cross-breeding, and MOET
Out-breeding is the breeding of unrelated animals and includes out-crossing, cross-breeding, and interspecific hybridisation. Cross-breeding mates superior males of one breed with superior females of another breed, yielding hybrids for direct commercial use or further inbreeding and selection to establish superior stable breeds. Both of these claims are true. In MOET, cows are administered hormones with FSH-like activity (not progesterone-like) to induce super ovulation of 6–8 eggs (not 1–2 eggs) per cycle, making that claim false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims defining a breed, classifying out-breeding methods, and describing cross-breeding outcomes are correct, whereas the claims denying inbreeding depression and misstating MOET hormones and egg counts are incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III are correct.
Statements I, III, and IV are correct.
Statements I, III, IV, and V are correct.
Statements II, IV, and V are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q03 - Plant breeding history Indian agriculture and resistant cultivars

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding plant breeding and disease/pest-resistant crop varieties:

Statement I: Recorded evidence of plant breeding dates back to 9,000–11,000 years ago, and all our major food crops today are derived from domesticated varieties.

Statement II: Agriculture accounts for approximately 62 per cent of India's GDP and employs nearly 33 per cent of the population.

Statement III: Pusa swarnim (Karan rai) is a Brassica variety resistant to white rust, and Pusa Sadabahar is a chilli variety resistant to chilli mosaic virus, tobacco mosaic virus, and leaf curl.

Statement IV: Wheat variety Himgiri is resistant to leaf and stripe rust and hill bunt, while Pusa A-4 is an okra variety resistant to shoot and fruit borer.

Statement V: Conventional breeding for disease resistance is never constrained by the limited availability of resistance genes in crop varieties or wild relatives.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant breeding has ancient roots in crop domestication and continues to underpin Indian agriculture through the development of high-yielding and disease- or pest-resistant cultivars.

Step 2: Evaluation of Plant Breeding History and Indian Agriculture Figures
Recorded evidence of plant breeding dates back 9,000–11,000 years, and all major food crops derive from domesticated varieties, making the first claim true. In India, agriculture accounts for approximately 33 per cent of GDP and employs nearly 62 per cent of the population; reversing these percentages makes the second claim false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Released Resistant Varieties and Breeding Constraints
Pusa swarnim (Karan rai) is a white-rust-resistant Brassica variety, and Pusa Sadabahar is a chilli variety resistant to chilli mosaic virus, tobacco mosaic virus, and leaf curl. Likewise, wheat variety Himgiri resists leaf and stripe rust and hill bunt, and okra variety Pusa A-4 resists shoot and fruit borer. Both of these claims are true. However, conventional breeding is often constrained by the limited number of disease resistance genes identified in crop varieties or wild relatives, making the claim that no such constraint exists false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the history of plant breeding and the specific resistant varieties of Brassica, chilli, wheat, and okra are correct, whereas the reversed GDP/employment figures and the denial of gene-availability constraints are incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III are correct.
Statements I, III, IV, and V are correct.
Statements I, III, and IV are correct.
Statements II, IV, and V are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q04 - Biofortification single cell protein and tissue culture

questiontext.text:
Assess the following five statements regarding biofortification, Single Cell Protein (SCP), and tissue culture:

Statement I: Breeding for improved nutritional quality is undertaken with the objectives of improving protein content and quality, oil content and quality, vitamin content, and micronutrient and mineral content.

Statement II: Wheat variety Atlas 66 has a high protein content, and IARI, New Delhi has released vitamin A enriched pumpkin and vitamin C enriched bathua and mustard.

Statement III: Because edible mushrooms are eaten by many people, it is impossible for microscopic fungi to ever become acceptable as food.

Statement IV: Micro-propagation produces thousands of genetically identical plants called somaclones in very short durations, and has been used commercially for tomato, banana, and apple.

Statement V: Selection amongst somaclonal variants and genetic engineering are also used in breeding for disease resistance alongside mutation breeding.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Modern crop improvement integrates biofortification for nutritional quality, microbial Single Cell Protein (SCP), and in vitro tissue culture techniques such as micro-propagation and somaclonal selection.

Step 2: Evaluation of Biofortification and Fungal SCP
Biofortification specifically targets improvements in protein content and quality, oil content and quality, vitamin content, and micronutrient and mineral content. Atlas 66 is a high-protein wheat donor, and IARI, New Delhi has released vitamin A enriched pumpkin as well as vitamin C enriched bathua and mustard. Both of these claims are true. In contrast, the widespread consumption of edible mushrooms and large-scale mushroom culture actually makes it believable—not impossible—that microscopic fungi too will become acceptable as food, making that claim false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Micro-propagation and Somaclonal Variants
Micro-propagation rapidly generates thousands of genetically identical plants called somaclones and has been applied commercially to tomato, banana, and apple. Additionally, selection amongst somaclonal variants and genetic engineering are used alongside mutation breeding to develop disease-resistant crops. Both of these claims are true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims covering biofortification objectives, Atlas 66 and IARI vegetable varieties, micro-propagation somaclones, and somaclonal/genetic-engineering disease resistance are correct, whereas the claim dismissing microscopic fungi as food is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and IV are correct.
Statements I, III, IV, and V are correct.
Statements I, II, IV, and V are correct.
